question: What is the main danger of ionizing radiation to human cells?
explanation: Ionizing radiation has enough energy to break chemical bonds, which harms the genetic material inside the cell nucleus. [learn more](BMP112_U6_T6#BMP112_U6_T6_h1)

question: Why should healthcare workers in Nigerian hospitals be careful about radiation exposure?

options.A: Radiation effects add up over time with ongoing exposure
options.B: Patients become radioactive and dangerous after a simple scan
options.C: Medical imaging units generate toxic chemical fumes daily
options.D: X-ray equipment frequently explodes if left plugged in

explanation: Even low doses of radiation can accumulate over years of clinical work, so safe handling practices are essential to prevent long-term cellular damage. [learn more](BMP112_U6_T6#BMP112_U6_T6_h1)

question: Which of these is NOT one of the three main rules of radiation protection?
explanation: The three foundational rules for staying safe around radiation are managing time, increasing distance, and using proper shielding. [learn more](BMP112_U6_T6#BMP112_U6_T6_h2)

question: How does stepping further away from an active mobile X-ray machine affect your radiation exposure?

options.A: It has no effect unless you wear a lead apron
options.B: It lowers your dose because radiation intensity drops with distance
options.C: It increases your dose because radiation bounces off walls
options.D: It stops all radiation waves instantly

explanation: Moving away from the source uses the inverse square law, making distance one of the best ways to reduce exposure. [learn more](BMP112_U6_T6#BMP112_U6_T6_h2)

question: What is the recommended annual radiation dose limit for a healthcare worker, averaged over five years?
explanation: Safety standards set the average annual occupational limit at 20 millisieverts to protect staff from long-term harm. [learn more](BMP112_U6_T6#BMP112_U6_T6_h3)

question: Why is there no fixed maximum dose limit for patients having X-ray procedures?

options.A: The government exempts all sick individuals from safety rules
options.B: Medical exposures are based on clinical need and kept as low as possible
options.C: Patients are naturally immune to radiation
options.D: Diagnostic imaging machines do not produce enough energy to harm patients

explanation: Patient imaging balances clinical benefit against risk, meaning the dose is tailored to what is necessary for diagnosis rather than a strict cutoff. [learn more](BMP112_U6_T6#BMP112_U6_T6_h3)

question: Where should a healthcare worker wear their radiation dosimeter badge during fluoroscopy?

options.A: Taped to the sole of their shoe
options.B: Inside the deepest pocket of their trousers
options.C: At the collar level outside the lead apron
options.D: Inside the lead apron to keep it hidden

explanation: Wearing the badge at the collar outside the apron measures exposure to unprotected areas like the thyroid and eyes. [learn more](BMP112_U6_T6#BMP112_U6_T6_h4)

question: What is the correct way to store lead aprons in a clinical department?

options.A: Rolled tightly into cylinders to save space
options.B: Draped over metal chairs or heavy equipment
options.C: Hung on specialized racks to prevent internal cracking
options.D: Folded neatly into a square on a shelf

explanation: Folding lead aprons causes the heavy protective core to crack over time, ruining its ability to block scatter radiation. [learn more](BMP112_U6_T6#BMP112_U6_T6_h4)

question: Why is confirming pregnancy status important before scheduling diagnostic imaging?

options.A: Embryonic cells divide rapidly and are very sensitive to radiation
options.B: X-ray beams will damage the imaging machine if a pregnant woman is scanned
options.C: Radiographers refuse to work without a signed certificate
options.D: Pregnant women are legally barred from radiology suites

explanation: Rapidly dividing embryonic tissues face a high risk of developmental issues if exposed to ionizing radiation. [learn more](BMP112_U6_T6#BMP112_U6_T6_h5)

question: What should a nurse do when a mobile X-ray machine is about to be used in a shared ward?

options.A: Stand beside the patient without any protective gear
options.B: Ask nearby patients and visitors to step back behind a screen
options.C: Turn off the ward's main electricity supply
options.D: Hold the X-ray cassette in place with bare hands

explanation: Clearing the surrounding area uses distance and physical barriers to protect bystanders from unnecessary scatter radiation. [learn more](BMP112_U6_T6#BMP112_U6_T6_h5)

question: Which agency is responsible for regulating radiation safety and licensing medical X-ray facilities in Nigeria?

options.A: Federal Ministry of Works and Housing
options.C: Nursing and Midwifery Council of Nigeria
options.D: National Agency for Food and Drug Administration and Control

explanation: The NNRA is the federal body responsible for setting safety standards, licensing equipment, and inspecting medical facilities in Nigeria. [learn more](BMP112_U6_T6#BMP112_U6_T6_h6)

question: Why do Nigerian hospitals appoint a Radiation Safety Officer (RSO)?

options.A: To repair broken circuit boards inside mobile imaging units
options.B: To operate every X-ray machine personally
options.C: To oversee equipment compliance, staff dose monitoring, and safety protocols
options.D: To handle patient billing for radiology services

explanation: The RSO ensures the facility maintains safety standards, tracks dosimeter badges, and keeps staff and patients safe. [learn more](BMP112_U6_T6#BMP112_U6_T6_h6)
